title: Epochal Rotor Preemptor: SLO-aware rotation and soft-preemption for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Continuous-batching workloads with mixed tenant priorities and diverse sequence lengths cause KV cache thrash and GPU memory pressure. Existing tranche/preemptors either kill requests abruptly (causing user-visible errors) or follow simple priority-queue schemes that starve low-volume tenants. We need an SLO-aware preemption policy that preserves tail latency SLOs for high-tier tenants, prevents KV cold-spike regressions, and minimizes unnecessary KV evictions that regen warmup cost.

Proposal: Implement an 'Epochal Rotor Preemptor' that cycles through tenant epochs (time-sliced fairness windows) and uses per-epoch credits + soft-preemption grace tokens to pause/resume microbatches. Core components: epoch rotation (round-robin with weighted slots by SLA tier), credit buckets per-tenant seeded by negotiated SLOs, soft-preempt handshake that signals worker to checkpoint KV/decoder state and yield micro-slices, and a compacting eviction covenant that favors preserving hot KV prefixes for a small preservation window after soft-resume. The preemptor coordinates with GPU memory headroom accounting and an admission controller that shrinks batch width proactively under KV-pressure.

Why different from past approaches: Instead of strict proportional-share or token-bucket eviction, rotor provides cyclical fairness guarantees that are robust to workload burstiness and long-running generative sessions. Soft-preemption reduces user visible regeneration while allowing rapid reclamation of GPU memory for higher-priority epochs. The compact eviction covenant mitigates cold-KV thrash by pinning recently used prefix blocks for a short epoch-window rather than evicting LRU immediately under pressure.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency SLO for P0 tenants remains within target under 95th percentile mixed workload runs (target: <= 1.5x baseline)
KV hit rate degradation <= 5% versus baseline when mixed with bursty long-sequence jobs
Tail preemptions (requests that required full restart) reduced by >= 70% compared to hard-kill preemptor in stress tests
No GPU OOMs in 48h continuous soak with synthetic mixed-tenancy traces
Canary rollout on dedicated pool with automated rollback if p99 SLO violations observed for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows
design_notes: Epoch length: configurable; baseline 250ms window (empirically chosen from p50/p95 sequence length distribution in logs). Tunable via runtime flag 'rotor.epoch_ms'.
Priority weighting: each tenant assigned weight w_i derived from SLA tier and recent token consumption rate. Rotor allocates epoch-slots proportional to w_i with min-slot floor to prevent starvation.

Credit model: two-layer credits: CPU-side admission credits (microbatch admission) and GPU-side residency credits (KV residency budget). Credits decay linearly each epoch; burst replenishment allowed up to a configurable cap.

Soft-preempt flow: preemptor signals worker with 'yield_request' containing grace_tokens=N; worker flushes current microbatch, checkpoints KV deltas and decoder state to ephemeral slot, releases GPU token and KV slack, then signals 'yield_ack'. Another epoch can then use the freed memory. If worker cannot yield within grace window, preemptor escalates to priority-backed hard reclaim (last resort).

KV preservation covenant: when a tenant is soft-resumed, the last K prefix blocks (configurable, default 8) are pinned for a preservation window (default 10s) to avoid cold restart penalties; eviction policy respects pinned blocks unless OOM imminent.

Admission shrinker: admission controller monitors KV occupancy ratio and slices batch width (max microbatch size) using an MLP-derived curve (trained offline) to maintain headroom target (e.g., 12% free GPU memory).

Telemetry: expose per-epoch metrics: epoch_utilization, yield_count, average_yield_latency, kv_pin_count, kv_hit_rate_by_epoch, preempt_escalations. Add tenant-level counters for credits, starving_time, and last_resume_ts.
State persistence: ephemeral checkpointing kept in-memory on host; long stalls tracked centrally so resumption attempts prioritize preserving tenant order.
decisions: Use soft-preemption with checkpoint/resume rather than immediate kill to preserve UX and reduce rerun compute cost.
Adopt epochal rotation (rotor) vs strict proportional fair-share because rotation reduces starvation during bursts and simplifies eviction heuristics.
Pin a small number of KV prefix blocks on resume to reduce cold-starts; cap pinned total to avoid uncontrolled memory growth.
Escalation to hard reclaim allowed but gated behind a configurable threshold ('rotor.escalation_threshold') and operator-visible alarms.
No immediate persistent storage of full KV on preempt; rely on short-term host memory and fast recompute to minimize I/O complexity.
Admission shrinker uses heuristic curve initially; plan to replace with online-learned policy after two iterations of A/B feedback.
risks: Incorrect epoch length tuning could increase perceived jitter for interactive requests — mitigate with auto-tuning and canary gradients.
Pinned KV blocks may lead to memory fragmentation over long runs — mitigation: periodic compaction and pin decay with aging policy.
Checkpoint/resume failure modes could increase tail if state reconstruction is delayed — add watchdog timers and fallback to graceful restart path.
Weight calculation can be gamed by tenants sending low-cost heartbeats; we will throttle heartbeat influence and validate with usage anomaly detectors.
Complexity increases operator burden for debugging — include detailed trace hooks and a dedicated console view for rotor epochs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for rotor scheduler state transitions and credit accounting.
Property tests that simulate extreme burst patterns to assert no starvation and bounded preemption escalations.
Integration tests in staging: attach synthetic multi-tenant trace (internal dataset /contrib/bench/mixed-tenancy-2025) and assert acceptance criteria across 24h run.
Chaos tests: random worker delay, delayed yield_ack, and KV eviction race to validate escalation correctness.
Performance microbench: measure checkpoint/resume overhead (target < 30ms median to resume small microbatches), and batch shrinker latency impact.
Load test with customer-like traces (redwood-corp/tenant-mix-2024) to ensure p99 stability.
Automated observability smoke: custom Grafana dashboard with rotor-specific panels and alert rules for p99 regressions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal dogfood): enable rotor on dev clusters with synthetic workloads, validate no functional regressions (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (canary): route 1% of traffic on dedicated pools to rotor-enabled runtime; monitor p99, kv_hit_rate, and yield_escalations for 48h.
Phase 2 (small-scale): increase to 10% on dedicated pools and run 7-day soak. If >2 SLO alerts in 24h, rollback and collect traces.
Phase 3 (roll-forward): 50% then full rollout with staged activation per region. Add runtime flag 'rotor.enable' for quick rollback.
Fallback: agent-side hard-kill policy is retained as last-resort; rollback document and postmortem playbook prepared.
